text:
maya: Heads-up — customer (acme-inc) updated their IdP mapping and our console preview shows ZERO effective roles for them after the change. They say they used the same mapping rule as before. anyone seen this?

sam: can you paste the mapping config they applied? also which preview endpoint they used (console vs API)? :eyes:

maya: pasted from support ticket (redacted tenant):
```yaml
mappings:
  - claim: "groups"
    regex: "^redwood-admins$"
    role: "tenant_admin"
```

maya: they clicked the console "preview mapping" and it returned empty list for effective roles.

dave: i pulled auth logs for that tenant — seeing a few 429s from our sso-preview service at the same time window. suspecting throttling + partial processing.

sam: 429s would definitely drop mapping evaluation in the current impl (we short-circuit on upstream rate limit). hmm. we should treat preview as best-effort but still return which rules were evaluated.

jen: this feels like a telemetry gap — we have SAML auth success/fail but no metric for "mapping evaluation failures" or "preview dropped". we also don't tag by mapping version. need counters: `saml.mapping.preview_failures` + `saml.mapping.evaluated_rules` with tenant_id.

li: from UX: the preview UI should show two panes — raw claims and matched rules + why a rule didn't match (regex mismatch, missing claim, evaluation skipped due to error). right now console just shows "no roles" which is scary for admins.

sam: quick API suggestion: preview endpoint returns { matched_rules: [...], unmatched_reasons: [...], effective_roles: [...] } so console can surface partial results even when backend had transient errors. example request: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"claims":["redwood-admins"]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sso/preview-map
```

sso-bot: alert: sso-preview service returned 429 for tenant acme-inc at 2024-04-15T14:12:03Z

sam: i'll add `matched_rules` and `unmatched_reasons` to the preview response. low-risk change — we can default to empty arrays. will also change server to NOT drop everything on 429; instead return partial with a `warning` field.

dave: i'll relax the rate limit for preview routes (separate quota bucket) and add a hard cap with a clear 429 message. we should avoid failing silently.

jen: also propose we add a canary rollout for the stricter changes (preview payload + rate-limit adjustments) behind a feature flag so enterprise tenants can opt-in first. add telemetry events for canary vs global.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature-flag/sso-preview-enhancements -> canary (10% tenants).

li: i'll sketch UI changes — show raw claims JSON, a rule-by-rule match table, and inline why a rule failed. will default to "unknown" state when preview had warning.

maya: action items:
- sam: implement preview payload fields + warning semantics (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- dave: create preview-specific rate-limit bucket + update 429 wording (ETA: +2d)
- jen: add `saml.mapping.preview_failures` metric and tag mapping_version, tenant_id (ETA: +3d)
- li: mock UI and small copy changes (ETA: next week)
- maya: notify customer with workaround (manual role assignment) and will follow up once canary is live

sam: one API detail to decide — do we return matched_rules as full rule objects (confidential -> maybe redact) or just rule_ids? leaning rule_ids + human_reason. thoughts?

jen: rule_ids + human_reason + metrics-friendly code sounds best. redact any regex or sensitive patterns.

maya: thanks all — this covers the immediate triage. please add PRs and link here when ready. :thumbsup:

sam: tagging @jen @li for final sign-off on metrics and UX before canary.

maya: adding follow-up note — we should also include the preview’s mapping_version in the audit logs so support can correlate later.

sso-bot: incident-note: SSO preview regression triaged, canary deploy scheduled.
